transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-15
Start: 14:00 ET
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Martin Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Veridian Head of Data), Laura Chen (Platform Lead), David Ortiz (Security)

Summary (auto): Initial POC scoping and commercial guardrails for pilot credits and path to procurement.

00:00 Martin Lee: Hey everybody, uh thanks for joining. I'm Martin from Redwood Inference, AE on this account. With me is Priya, our SE.
00:12 Samir Patel: Hi all, Samir here. Thanks for doing this. We're hoping to scope a pilot to validate latency and cost for our fraud-detection enrichment flows.
00:22 Priya Nair: Great, quick agenda — success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, then commercial/pilot terms and procurement path. Sound good?
00:29 Laura Chen: Yep, that's what we need. Quick note — platform constraints: most requests are ~512 tokens, a 95th p99 latency target of 150ms for the critical path.
00:42 Martin Lee: OK that helps. When you say 150ms p99 are you measuring from app to token or just the inference piece?
00:49 Laura Chen: App to token end-to-end, so network plus inference. We can carve out inference SLO — ideally <100ms p99.
01:02 Samir Patel: Our peak traffic is about 350 qps for the enrichment pipeline, but that's bursty — sustained is closer to 120 qps. Typical seq lengths: 64 tokens median, 512 for some larger requests.
01:20 Priya Nair: Good, that's helpful. For the POC we usually ask for a representative slice — can you share a 24-48 hour dump or synthetic traces? It helps set batching and latency targets.
01:31 Samir Patel: Yeah, we can share anonymized traces. We'll need an NDA addendum? David, thoughts?
01:38 David Ortiz: We have a standard DPA in place with Redwood, but for sample data we want to sanitize PII. We'll coordinate with Samir. Procurement will want the SOC2 docs too.
01:50 Martin Lee: We'll attach the SOC 2 and our private deployment docs. On the commercial side — typical pilot setup is: we provide $X in credits, pilot term 4 weeks evaluation window, with an optional extension. There's a usage cap and we agree on success criteria up front.
02:06 Laura Chen: Can you be more specific on credits and caps? We need to show finance what the runway looks like.
02:12 Martin Lee: Sure — our standard is $20k credits for a 4-week pilot for accounts this size. That generally covers benchmark runs and initial traffic. We can tier up if you want a longer run. The credits apply to hosted API usage; for private or dedicated there's a different model — usually reserved capacity discussion.
02:28 Samir Patel: We might need a private deployment later due to data residency, but for the POC hosted is fine if we have strong guarantees and the ability to move to dedicated. How do you handle fallbacks if capacity is constrained?
02:41 Priya Nair: We have smart routing and fallbacks to compatible model variants. For the pilot we'll pin a model and config. We also recommend a KV cache/prefix cache for the enrichment flows to hit cache often — that materially reduces cost.
02:55 Laura Chen: On the model side — are you verifying the open model performance? We run exact-match vs our ground truth.
03:02 Priya Nair: Yes, part of the benchmark plan includes quality evals: we ask you to provide a labeled sample or scoring rubric. We'll run our eval harness and share per-step metrics: latency, throughput, tokens/cost, and quality delta vs baseline.
03:18 Samir Patel: Baseline for us is an in-house distilled model — cost is low but accuracy degrades on certain edge cases. We'll provide examples.
03:26 Martin Lee: For commercial guardrails: credits, pilot term, and a clear pass/fail criteria — e.g., p99 inference <100ms, cost per inference <$0.003 at target qps, and accuracy within 2% of baseline on measured tests. Does that map to what you expect?
03:43 Laura Chen: That seems reasonable. Need to confirm the cost target with finance but the SLOs look right.
03:50 David Ortiz: Procurement will also want to see retention and encryption details — KMS, HSM support, and audit logging.
03:58 Priya Nair: We'll include KMS integration docs and our audit log guarantees. For private deployment we can show options for customer-managed KMS and VPC peering.
04:10 Samir Patel: Timeline question — if POC is successful, what's the path to procurement and contracting? We have a standard IT procurement cycle that takes 6-8 weeks.
04:20 Martin Lee: Typical path: pilot -> procurement/PO conversion -> reserved capacity or enterprise contract. We'll work with you to fast-track procurement: provide standard SOW, pricing, and security pack. We can do interim terms to allow production ramp while final contract is negotiated.
04:36 Laura Chen: Any examples of pricing bands for reserved capacity?
04:40 Martin Lee: We can include an indicative pricing range in the proposal — depends on committed throughput and model family. For now pilot credits let you validate unit economics.
04:49 Samir Patel: Benchmarks — can Redwood run a benchmark in our environment or do we run on your hosted infra?
04:55 Priya Nair: We can do both. For hosted we'll run a Redwood-managed benchmark. If you want to mimic production network and data residency we can run a private benchmark runner that you deploy (we'll provide a container + scripts). The benchmark plan will capture seq length distribution, concurrency, warmup, and metrics to capture p50/p95/p99 latencies and tokens/cost.
05:15 Samir Patel: That sounds good. We want the benchmark to reflect 75th/95th percentile loads. Also include cold-start/kv-cache warmup behavior.
05:26 Priya Nair: Absolutely — we'll include warmup and cache priming steps. For the pilot credits, note that long benchmark runs can exhaust credits; we'll size the plan to fit $20k but can scope heavier runs as an add-on.
05:40 Martin Lee: On procurement path — we should introduce our contracts rep to your procurement once you sign off on the POC terms. That usually shortens the 6-8 week loop.
05:50 David Ortiz: One more security ask: can you provide a list of sub-processors and a data flow diagram?
05:55 Priya Nair: Yes, we'll attach the sub-processor list and a sanitized dataflow.
06:02 Samir Patel: OK next steps — we'll send traces, Redwood sends proposal and benchmark plan, schedule bench run week of 2/23. Anything else?
06:10 Martin Lee: We'll also throw in the SOC2 and private deployment docs. I'll include the pilot credit and the explicit pass/fail success criteria in the proposal.
06:18 Laura Chen: If finance needs a statement of work to release payment for credits, can you provide a templated SOW?
06:23 Martin Lee: Yes, we'll include a templated SOW and agreement for the pilot.
06:28 David Ortiz: Procurement will want to know if we can get a limited liability cap for the pilot period — usually ok, but we'll surface that early.
06:35 Martin Lee: Noted. We'll flag procurement and legal to discuss liability and procurement triggers.
06:40 Samir Patel: Thanks everyone. This is helpful. We'll get the traces over and confirm dates.
06:45 Martin Lee: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the proposal and benchmark plan by Tuesday.
06:50 (call ends)
notes: Pilot credits: proposed $20k for 4-week pilot (hosted) — covers benchmark + initial traffic
Success criteria proposed: inference p99 <100ms, cost/inference < $0.003, accuracy within 2% of baseline
Benchmark plan: include warmup + cache priming, p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/cost, quality evals
Procurement: expected 6-8 weeks but Redwood to provide SOW and engage procurement to accelerate
